Discrete distributions chapter

Discrete distributions: scientific, instructional and visual review

Delivery status

This is an English review draft under the student's standing continuous-authoring instruction. Student approval is not inferred. The chapter is delivered only after its recorded checks pass; publication is recorded separately.

Scope and source comparison

The full lesson covers experiment contracts; Bernoulli and binomial laws; factorial moments and PGFs; conditional subsets, thinning and competing labels; independent unequal trials; geometric conventions, survival, memorylessness, censoring and discrete races; negative-binomial stopping, convolution, modes and real-shape normalization; hypergeometric support, finite-population dependence and marked-position waiting; Poisson laws, units, splitting, random intensities and approximation; stable computation; and uniform transformed lattices.

Four core courses from Oxford, Cambridge, Berkeley and MIT were genuinely read. Stanford's reviewed written Poisson slides provide a fifth university comparison. Nine candidate universities appear in the bounded selection register. Acquiring a PDF or reading a course inventory is not counted as reading its chapter. Source mistakes and differing conventions are explicitly reconciled, including tied Poisson modes, effective hypergeometric support and finite versus infinitesimal process intervals.

Problems and final notes

There are 85 independently explained original or reconstructed medium-to-hard formula/concept questions and three authenticated Iranian examination bridges, totaling 88 worked entries. Every original entry has a complete teaching solution and a documented decision about a companion figure. Three reconstructed exercise types identify their Oxford or Cambridge structural origin; their wording, parameters and explanations are independently written. All three authentic questions are explicitly revisited archive entries. Original PDF page images, immutable commit, hashes and printed option order were checked; answers are independently derived, not presented as official keys.

The 84 final rules use complete sentences and distinguish assumptions, support, boundaries, conditional laws, exact probabilities, approximation scales and numerical evaluation. They complement the main proofs rather than replace them.

Independent scientific evidence

s_distributions-evidence/mathematics.json records exhaustive independent enumeration of 594 experiments, checks of all 358 stored checkpoints, 105 cases against the actual editable JavaScript law calculator, and named numerical answer checks. Enumeration includes fixed-horizon Bernoulli sequences, uniform subsets and marked-position order statistics. The waiting-player oracle enumerates full trial paths rather than calling the player's dynamic program. Finite enumeration is evidence for these instantiated models; the teaching body supplies the general proofs.

The native MathML audit rejects unbalanced fences and standalone closing-delimiter script bases. Exact counts are stored in the latest evidence, so a later manuscript correction does not leave an invented count here. Formula text was also reviewed for missing TeX command boundaries. Real-shape negative-binomial normalization and finite-gap moment calculations were expanded into derivations rather than left as table assertions.

Visual and interaction evidence

Twenty-six compact mechanism-specific models provide 358 checkpoints and 66 placements across teaching and worked solutions. They distinguish exact mass transfer, absorbing completion, finite-population depletion, subset enumeration, observation mapping, joint allocation, law prefixes, rare-count comparison and lattice transformations. Partial destination mass, incomplete enumeration and omitted infinite tails are labeled. Prefixes are never silently normalized. The editable laboratory displays five law families and preserves its preceding valid result after invalid input.

The Edge audit checks every frame's geometry, padding, bounds and unique moving entities; STIX Two Math, Newsreader, Source Sans 3 and JetBrains Mono; actual transition, pause/resume, previous/next, slider, before/after comparison, reduced motion, print, mobile containment, runtime errors, library route and weekly link. Representative desktop and mobile screenshots were also visually inspected. A label crossing a mass-transfer arrow and a label crossing affine-map arrows were repositioned following that inspection. Final verification is repeated after those corrections.

Retention and limits

All 57 previous chapter pages are compared byte-for-byte with the pre-chapter baseline. Their completed content is preserved. The library now has 58 chapter pages and 4001 worked-problem entries; repeated authentic questions are not counted as distinct archive discoveries.

No exhaustive review of all courses worldwide, literal perfection or guaranteed performance on every unseen question is asserted. The stated chapter boundary is reviewed; general continuous laws, estimation, stochastic processes and infinite-series topics beyond these derived count-law identities are handled in subsequent chapters. Floating-point laboratory values may have rounding error; finite display limits are explicit and do not change a law's full support.
